questions.q: In evaluating a binary classifier, the confusion matrix shows \( TP = 45 \), \( TN = 40 \), \( FP = 10 \), and \( FN = 10 \). Compute the overall classification accuracy.
questions.answer: Accuracy is the ratio of correct predictions to total samples: \( \text{Accuracy} = \frac{TP + TN}{TP + TN + FP + FN} = \frac{45 + 40}{105} = \frac{85}{105} = 81.0\% \).

questions.q: A spam classification model identifies \( TP = 30 \) genuine spam emails and \( FP = 10 \) legitimate emails falsely flagged as spam. What is the precision of this model?
questions.answer: Precision is the fraction of predicted positive instances that are truly positive: \( \text{Precision} = \frac{TP}{TP + FP} = \frac{30}{30 + 10} = \frac{30}{40} = 75.0\% \).
